arxiv-2103-10335.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Regional Net-load with Conditional Extremes and Gridded NWP
arxiv-2103-10335.creator: Jethro Browell and Matteo Fasiolo
arxiv-2103-10335.description: Abstract The increasing penetration of embedded renewables makes forecasting net-load, consumption less embedded generation, a significant and growing challenge. Here a framework for producing probabilistic forecasts of net-load is proposed with particular attention given to the tails of predictive distributions, which are required for managing risk associated with low-probability events.

arxiv-2306-00092.title: Accretion onto disk galaxies via hot and rotating CGM inflows 2020 Accretion onto disk galaxies via hot and rotating CGM inflows –
arxiv-2306-00092.creator: Jonathan Stern, Drummond Fielding, Zachary Hafen, Kung-Yi Su, Nadav Naor, Claude-André Faucher-Giguère, Eliot Quataert and James Bullock, School of Physics & Astronomy, Tel Aviv University, Tel Aviv 69978, Israel Center for Computational Astrophysics, Flatiron Institute, 162 Fifth Avenue, New York,
arxiv-2306-00092.description: Abstract Observed accretion rates onto the Milky-Way and other local spirals fall short of that required to sustain star formation for cosmological timescales. A potential avenue for this unseen accretion is a rotating inflow in the volume-filling hot phase ( ∼ 10 6 ​ K \sim 10^{6}\,{\rm K} ) of the circumgalactic medium (CGM), as suggested by some cosmological simulations.

arxiv-2306-07466.title: Statistical Methods for Auditing the Quality of Manual Content Reviews
arxiv-2306-07466.creator: Xuan Yang, Andrew Smart, Daniel Theron
arxiv-2306-07466.description: Abstract Large technology firms face the problem of moderating content on their online platforms for compliance with laws and policies. To accomplish this at the scale of billions of pieces of content per day, a combination of human and machine review are necessary to label content.

arxiv-2307-12418.title: HateModerate: Testing Hate Speech Detectors against Content Moderation Policies Warning: this paper discusses and contains content that can be offensive or upsetting.
arxiv-2307-12418.creator: Jiangrui Zheng, Xueqing Liu, Guanqun Yang, Mirazul Haque, Xing Qian, Ravishka Rathnasuriya, Wei Yang, Girish Budhrani, Stevens Institute of Technologyjzheng36,xliu127,xqian7,gyang16,gbudhran@stevens.edu, University of Texas at Dallasmirazul.haque,ravishka.rathnasuriya,wei.yang@utdallas.edu
arxiv-2307-12418.description: Abstract To protect users from massive hateful content, existing works studied automated hate speech detection. Despite the existing efforts, one question remains: do automated hate speech detectors conform to social media content policies? A platform’s content policies are a checklist of content moderated by the social media platform.

arxiv-2402-05023.title: On the Exact Linearization of Minimally Underactuated Configuration Flat Lagrangian Systems in Generalized State Representation This research was funded in whole, or in part, by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) P36473. For the purpose of open access, the author has applied a CC BY public copyright li
arxiv-2402-05023.creator: Georg Hartl, Conrad Gstöttner, Bernd Kolar, Markus Schöberl
arxiv-2402-05023.description: Abstract In this paper, we examine the exact linearization of configuration flat Lagrangian control systems in generalized state representation with p p degrees of freedom and p − 1 p-1 control inputs by quasi-static feedback of its generalized state. We formally introduce generalized Lagrangian control systems, which are obtained when configuration variables are considered as inputs instead of forces.

arxiv-2404-07746.title: Scenario Reduction with Guarantees for Stochastic Optimal Control of Linear Systems
arxiv-2404-07746.creator: Francesco Cordiano, Bart De Schutter
arxiv-2404-07746.description: Abstract Scenario reduction algorithms can be an effective means to provide a tractable description of the uncertainty in optimal control problems. However, they might significantly compromise the performance of the controlled system. In this paper, we propose a method to compensate for the effect of scenario reduction on stochastic optimal control problems for chance-constrained linear systems with additive uncertainty.

arxiv-2407-11504.title: Bootstrapped Pre-training with Dynamic Identifier Prediction for Generative Retrieval
arxiv-2407-11504.creator: Yubao Tang Ruqing Zhang Jiafeng Guo Maarten de Rijke, Yixing Fan Xueqi Cheng
arxiv-2407-11504.description: Abstract Generative retrieval uses differentiable search indexes to directly generate relevant document identifiers in response to a query. Recent studies have highlighted the potential of a strong generative retrieval model, trained with carefully crafted pre-training tasks, to enhance downstream retrieval tasks via fine-tuning.

arxiv-2411-07007.title: Non-Adversarial Inverse Reinforcement Learning via Successor Feature Matching
arxiv-2411-07007.creator: Arnav Kumar Jain Harley Wiltzer Jesse Farebrother, Irina Rish Glen Berseth Sanjiban Choudhury
arxiv-2411-07007.description: Abstract In inverse reinforcement learning (IRL), an agent seeks to replicate expert demonstrations through interactions with the environment. Traditionally, IRL is treated as an adversarial game, where an adversary searches over reward models, and a learner optimizes the reward through repeated RL procedures. This game-solving approach is both computationally expensive and difficult to stabilize.

arxiv-2503-11453.title: Do Comments and Expertise Still Matter? An Experiment on Programmers’ Adoption of AI-Generated JavaScript Code
arxiv-2503-11453.creator: Changwen Li, Christoph Treude, Ofir Turel
arxiv-2503-11453.description: Abstract This paper investigates the factors influencing programmers’ adoption of AI-generated JavaScript code recommendations within the context of lightweight, function-level programming tasks. It extends prior research by (1) utilizing objective (as opposed to the typically self-reported) measurements for programmers’ adoption of AI-generated code and (2) examining whether AI-generated comments added to code recommendations and development expertise drive AI-generated code adoption.

pmc-10611453.description: PurposeThis study aims to investigate the effect and feasibility of intra-aortic catheter looping via transradial access in angioplasty for symptomatic intracranial severe (>70%) atherosclerotic stenosis or occlusion of large arteries (SISOLAs).Materials and methodsPatients with SISOLAs who underwent transradial endovascular angioplasty using the catheter looping technique in the ascending aorta were retrospectively enrolled. The clinical data and treatment outcomes were analyzed.

pmc-11416536.title: Protocol for a personalized (N-of-1) trial for testing the effects of a mind–body intervention on sleep duration in middle-aged women working in health care
pmc-11416536.creator: Ashley M. Goodwin, Codruta Chiuzan, Ciaran P. Friel, Danielle Miller, Jordyn Rodillas, Joan Duer-Hefele, Ying Kuen Cheung, Karina W. Davidson
pmc-11416536.description: BackgroundAdequate sleep plays a crucial role in maintaining physical, mental, and emotional health. On average, adults require 7–9 h of sleep per night. However, less than two-thirds of women meet this recommendation. During the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, poor sleep quality and moderate-to-severe stress were highly prevalent among healthcare workers (HCWs), especially women.

pmc-12553171.title: Therapeutic effects of cinnamic acid in a rat model of collagenase-induced Achilles tendinopathy
pmc-12553171.creator: Sercan Capkin, Ali Ihsan Kilic, Saadet Ozen Akarca Dizakar, Yagmur Isin
pmc-12553171.description: BackgroundAchilles tendinopathy is a common degenerative disorder characterized by pain, impaired function, and poor tissue regeneration. Effective treatment remains a challenge due to the tendon’s limited healing capacity. Cinnamic acid, a naturally occurring phenolic compound, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects in various tissue repair models.

pmc-12607625.title: Principles of bacteriostatic and bactericidal antibiotics at subinhibitory concentrations
pmc-12607625.creator: Elizabeth Vaisbourd, David Shaanan Glass, Yifan Yang, Avi Mayo, Anat Bren, Uri Alon
pmc-12607625.description: Subinhibitory antibiotic exposures are common in clinical and environmental contexts, yet their effects on bacterial growth dynamics remain incompletely understood. We studied the temporal response of Escherichia coli to a panel of bactericidal (“cidal”) and bacteriostatic (“static”) antibiotics at sub-minimum inhibitory concentrations (sub-MIC). We uncover a sharp dynamical distinction between the two classes.

pmc-13468207.title: Further Investigations on Natural and Synthetic Bis-(1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline) Derivatives Interacting with the Apamin-Sensitive Site of Small-Conductance Calcium-Activated Potassium Channels

pmc-13468207.description: Our previous study demonstrated that bis-(1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline) (bis-THIQ) compounds such as tetrandrine and AG525E1 exhibit significant affinity for SK channels. Interestingly, the stereoisomers of AG525 display markedly different affinities toward SK channels, with the (S,S) stereoisomer being the best ligand. Previous structure-based in silico investigations failed to provide a satisfactory explanation for these differences.
